clue.text: Dismiss whole cricket team in like manner? Some game!

definitions.text: Dismiss whole cricket team in like manner?
definitions.note: a verb phrase: to take all ten wickets with catches

blocks.clueFragment: Dismiss whole cricket team in like manner?
blocks.note: a side is all out when ten wickets fall, so catching all ten dismisses it
second meaning: an old card game, also called Scotch whist

explanation.walkthrough: A cricket side has eleven players but is all out after ten wickets, which is why the number is ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Catch-the-ten is the name of a Scottish trick-taking card game, so it is literally a game.

clue.text: Genetic mapping measure: men with tic distorted body part (11, two words)

indicators.note: distorted means twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first letters to rearrange
joined with the previous word in the rearrangement
an organ is a part of the body

explanation.surface: Sounds like a geneticist describing men whose twitch has deformed part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A centimorgan is the unit of distance on a genetic map, so it measures gene positions.

clue.text: Leg visible below eagle with no tail wind

indicators.note: with no tail means the end is cut off, so the last letter goes
in a down answer, below puts the first-named piece under the second

blocks.note: aquila is Latin for eagle, also the constellation
the on side in cricket is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: A bird-watcher spotting a tailless eagle's leg in a strong breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, leg and on both name the side of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquilon is the poetic name for the north wind, from the Latin Aquilo.

clue.text: Trend was limiting by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says to go by how the phrase is pronounced, not spelt

blocks.note: tied means bound or restricted, a past tense matching was limiting

explanation.surface: A commentator suggesting a fashion seemed restrictive.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide of opinion is its general drift or direction, the same as a trend.

clue.text: Horse or coley supplied by cookroom on board

blocks.note: first meaning: a donkey or small horse, in Scots
second meaning: a young coalfish
third meaning: a small cabin or galley on a boat

explanation.surface: A ship's galley serving up either horsemeat or fish.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition. Coley is the coalfish, a cheap white fish common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuddy is a dialect word for a donkey, a name for the young coalfish, and a small ship's cabin or galley.

clue.text: Much-prized grass? Get a guard when it's vandalized (9, two words)

indicators.note: vandalized means smashed and wrecked, so the letters before it are thrown out of order

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A groundsman protecting a prized lawn from vandals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is slang for cannabis; dagga is the South African word for it, and true dagga is cannabis itself as against wild dagga.
explanation.definitionFit: True dagga is the South African name for cannabis, slang grass that its users prize.

clue.text: Group of Carthusians in Romanian town

indicators.note: a group of letters taken out of a longer word, as some of its members

blocks.note: four letters lifted from inside the monks' name

explanation.surface: A community of Carthusian monks settled in a town in Romania.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carthusians are a monastic order; their name holds the town Husi.
explanation.definitionFit: Husi (Huși) is a town in north-eastern Romania, known for its wine.

clue.text: Cover for mattress that's chewed up inside — might it transfix a kipper?

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the letters climb, so the word is read backwards
inside places the turned letters within the mattress word

blocks.note: ticking, or a tick, is the strong cloth case of a mattress
something chewed is something ate, in the past tense

explanation.surface: A mattress cover gnawed through, and a question about spearing a smoked fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A kipper is a smoked herring, but also a kipper tie, the very wide 1970s necktie. 'Kipper' wants to be the fish; it is the tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie tack is a pin pushed through a necktie to hold it in place, so it could pierce a kipper tie.

clue.text: Gas was upsetting for very young one

blocks.note: neon is a noble gas
as in 'what's eating you?': if something ate you it was upsetting you

explanation.surface: A gas was harmful to a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was upsetting' is the past of 'eat' in its 'trouble, bother' sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A neonate is a newborn infant, the youngest kind of child.

clue.text: Bertie's club bar reduced dram units

indicators.note: bar means except or without, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: Bertie Wooster belongs to the Drones Club in P. G. Wodehouse's stories
dr is the shortened form, or abbreviation, of dram

explanation.surface: Bertie's club bar has cut the size of its whisky measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like the drinks counter but means 'except'. A dram is a small measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Ones are units: in arithmetic the units column is the ones column.

clue.text: With cred in New York a long way ahead of the market?

indicators.note: ahead of puts the first piece in front of the next one

blocks.note: as in 'streets ahead', by a long way
a mart is a market

explanation.surface: Someone with credibility in New York is well ahead of the financial markets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In New York' marks the American word; the British say streetwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Street-smart is the American term for streetwise, having the street cred to cope with city life.

clue.text: Strange U-turn round threshold it was distinctly wayward

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, unruliness; 'it was' marks an obsolete word

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged
round says the rearranged letters go around the next piece of wordplay

blocks.note: taken letter for letter, hyphen dropped
limen is the psychologist's word for a threshold

explanation.surface: An odd U-turn swung around a doorway by someone behaving very erratically.
explanation.walkthrough: UNRUT wraps LIMEN to give UNRULIMENT, Spenser's word for unruliness. The definition is loose: 'it was' flags an obsolete word for being wayward.
explanation.definitionFit: Unruliment is an archaic noun for unruliness, the state of being headstrong and wayward.

clue.text: Having nothing on, turned brownish, incomplete change in colour

definitions.note: the answer is a noun used in the phrase 'in the nuddy', meaning naked

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the colour word is read backwards
incomplete means lacking its end, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown
to dye something changes its colour

explanation.surface: Someone stripped off, went brown in the sun, and their tan is patchy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stretches: NUDDY is informal for nakedness, used in 'in the nuddy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the nuddy is a jokey British phrase for being naked, wearing no clothes at all.

clue.text: Wind? Anonymous harangue contains tons

indicators.note: contains says the rant word holds the next letter within it

blocks.note: a shortening of anon, short for anonymous
a tirade is a long angry speech
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: Is an unsigned rant full of tonnage just so much hot air?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind?' looks like a jibe at the rant but is the definition: an antitrade is a wind above, and opposite to, a trade wind.
explanation.definitionFit: An antitrade is an upper-air wind blowing counter to the trade winds beneath it.

clue.text: Healthy creature down under, female roo, right?

blocks.note: a female kangaroo is a doe
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An Australian admiring a fit-looking female kangaroo and checking they have it right.
explanation.walkthrough: In Australian and New Zealand usage a doer is an animal that thrives, a 'good doer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian farmers call a beast that grows and stays well a doer, so it is a thriving animal there.

clue.text: Means of decorating fabric that is initially dipped in trough

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows
in places the preceding letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: a tye is a trough for washing ore
i.e. stands for id est, Latin for 'that is'
the opening letter of dipped

explanation.surface: Describes a fabric printing method where cloth is first dunked in a trough of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: TYE is a mining word for a trough where ore is washed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tie-dyeing patterns cloth by knotting it before dyeing, so it is a way of decorating material.

clue.text: English, following how decimalization works, concentrated

indicators.note: following says the first-named letter comes after the phrase next to it

blocks.note: decimal money and measures work in tens
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A remark about Britain's switch to decimal currency and how it changed English habits.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'in tens' is read as one run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense and concentrated both describe something strong, focused or undiluted.

clue.text: Like some fish? One's shredded it to put inside another one

indicators.note: shredded means torn to pieces, so the letters that follow are scrambled
put inside places the scrambled letters within the next item

blocks.note: another fish, picking up 'some fish' from the definition
the letters to scramble

explanation.surface: An angler explaining that one fish has been chopped up and stuffed inside another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another one' means another fish, since the definition is about fish. The scrambled letters go between the O and D of that fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Cottoid means belonging to the sculpin family, Cottidae, which includes the bullhead.

clue.text: Mystical charm, one representation of Christ held by converted Arabs

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged
held by means gripped inside, so one letter sits within the rearranged word

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
a, the indefinite article, means one
X is the Greek chi, the first letter of Christos

explanation.surface: A Christian symbol kept as a magical amulet by Arabs who have converted.
explanation.walkthrough: The chi-rho monogram and the X of Xmas both use chi, the Greek letter written X, for Christ.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraxas is a Gnostic mystic word engraved on gems worn as amulets, so it names a charm.

clue.text: Down with entering calendar info in file collection!

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so this phrase sits within the next item

blocks.note: a calendar tells you the date
French a bas, 'down with', as in protest slogans

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry against having to log appointments in yet another set of files.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down with' is the French slogan a bas, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A database is an organised store of records, which is a collection of computer files.

clue.text: Single wave came to land, breaking early

indicators.note: breaking means bursting into, so the first phrase goes inside the word that follows

blocks.note: soon means before long, early
lit means alighted, as a bird lands

explanation.surface: A lone wave rolled ashore and broke before expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' suggests surf; it means the landing word breaks into the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A soliton is a solitary wave that keeps its shape and speed as it travels.

clue.text: What comes from cattle is only half fine for Boers

indicators.note: only half keeps just one of the two letters of the little word before it

blocks.note: the sound cows make
the first of its two letters

explanation.surface: Seems to say that something cattle produce is only half acceptable to South African farmers.
explanation.walkthrough: Boers are Afrikaans-speaking South Africans, so 'for Boers' asks for the Afrikaans word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooi is South African slang from Afrikaans meaning nice, pleasant or good.

clue.text: Simple Scottish dance (though I don't accept the form it takes)

blocks.note: ba is the Scots form of ball, a formal dance

blocks.clueFragment: (though I don't accept the form it takes)
blocks.note: sic is printed after a quoted form to show it is copied as found, not endorsed

explanation.surface: A plain Highland dance, mentioned by someone who disapproves of how it is performed.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket is not an aside: it is a description of the editorial [sic]. The Scots ba is a ball, here the dance kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic and simple both mean plain, elementary, without elaboration.

clue.text: Steer children in the wrong direction

indicators.note: going the wrong direction means running backwards, right to left

blocks.note: tots are small children

explanation.surface: An instruction to lead young people astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like a verb but is the noun: a young castrated bull.
explanation.definitionFit: Stot is a northern and Scots word for a bullock, which is what a steer is.

clue.text: Sticking to schedule (not great when it's broken) (8, two words)

indicators.note: a broken thing is smashed up, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A wry comment that keeping to a timetable is no fun once the timetable has fallen apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A project on target is meeting its planned deadlines and goals, so it is keeping to schedule.

clue.text: Guys taking tea on board?

indicators.note: taking means holding inside, so the next letters go within the ship

blocks.note: SS, steamship, and words 'on board' sit between its letters
tay is an Irish and dialect form of tea

explanation.surface: Asks whether some men are having tea aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guys' looks like men but means ropes; 'on board' is the crossword convention of going inside SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Guys and stays are both ropes or wires that brace a mast or pole.

clue.text: Despicable types in wretched togs to be advised Garb sat badly

indicators.note: badly means done wrong, so the letters are set in a muddled order

linkWords: in wretched togs to be advised

blocks.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Scruffy rogues in shabby clothes who sat about badly dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The working is 'Garb sat badly'. The words 'in wretched togs to be advised' add nothing to the wordplay; the source text seems to carry a stray fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratbag is Australian and British slang for a nasty or contemptible person.

clue.text: Indication of dismay in balloon, say, part of which gradually rises

definitions.text: Indication of dismay in balloon, say

indicators.note: part of means a fragment of the following words, so the letters lie within them
in a down answer, rises means reading upwards, so the run is reversed

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A cartoon speech bubble, or a hot-air balloon slowly rising, signalling alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: The balloon is a comic-strip speech bubble, where cries like this are written.
explanation.definitionFit: Argh is an exclamation of frustration or dismay, typically lettered in comic strip bubbles.

clue.text: Time of day to witness lake

blocks.note: to witness something is to see it
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A tourist choosing an hour to go and view a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: SEEL is an old dialect word for a season or time, as in 'the seel of the day'.
explanation.definitionFit: In old northern dialect seel means a season or period, so the seel of the day is its time.

clue.text: Soak on edge put in order for second time.

definitions.text: put in order for second time

indicators.note: on places the first word directly against the next one in the row

blocks.note: to ret flax is to soak it
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: Seems to tell someone to soak a hem before tidying it again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soak' is the verb ret, used of flax and hemp; the clue also leads into the next across clue, where a soak is a drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim is to make neat or put in order, and RE- means doing it again.

clue.text: Gap year? No indeed, aim to get working

indicators.note: no means without, so the word for indeed is taken away
getting something working means putting it in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
yea means yes, indeed; it is the part to remove
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone rejects a gap year and is told to get a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gap year' looks like one phrase, but 'Gap' is the definition and 'year' the start of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Rima is the anatomical word for a slit or cleft, such as the opening between the vocal cords.

clue.text: …For this? It makes most of stomach turn

definitions.note: reads on from the previous clue: what a soak on edge craves

indicators.note: most of means all but the last part, so the final letter goes
turn means flip round, so the remaining letters run backwards

blocks.note: the gorge is the throat or stomach, as in 'makes one's gorge rise'

explanation.surface: Continues the previous clue: a drinker is twitchy for something whose taste would turn your stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots pick up 'Soak on edge' from 29: a soak, a heavy drinker, is on edge for drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Grog is rum and water, or any strong drink, which is what a heavy drinker longs for.

clue.text: Aunt's diner toying with this — in Indian restaurant?

indicators.note: toying with means playing about, so the letters are jumbled together

blocks.note: letters that join the answer in the mix but do not appear in it
this stands for the answer itself, joined to the other letters

explanation.surface: An aunt fiddling with something on her plate at a curry house.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus the aunt's letters rearrange to INDIAN RESTAURANT. As printed one N is missing; 'dinner' would make it exact.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is a cooling yoghurt side dish served with curries, so it is found in Indian restaurants.

clue.text: A fool's time occupied in silly delay, showing disturbance

indicators.note: something occupied in a place is inside it, so one letter goes within the next word
silly means foolish and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
git is British slang for a fool
T is the abbreviation for time
the letters to jumble, with the time letter added

explanation.surface: An idiot's timing is upset by a pointless hold-up, and it shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool's' is GIT plus 's read as 'has': the fool has time held in a jumbled delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something agitatedly means doing it in a flustered, disturbed way.

clue.text: Is suit in stand out of place? It was irritating, for sure

definitions.note: 'it was' marks an obsolete adjective meaning unpleasant

indicators.note: in puts the legal word inside the letters of the following words
out of place means misplaced, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
a plea is a lawsuit or legal action
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks whether a smart suit looks wrong at a stall, and admits it was annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' is the lawsuit sense, not clothing. 'It was ... for sure' marks an obsolete word, since displeasant has dropped out of use.
explanation.definitionFit: Displeasant is an old word for unpleasant, causing annoyance or displeasure.
